scope.user_request: Create and review an educational storyboard explaining how a ribosome reads mRNA, tRNA recognizes codons, and a polypeptide extends step by step; identify organism-specific initiation simplifications.
included: Ribosome decoding of mRNA into a polypeptide
Initiation complex formation with organism-specific features (bacterial 30S/50S, fMet-tRNA, Shine-Dalgarno; eukaryotic 40S/60S, Met-tRNAi)
Elongation cycle: A-site entry, peptide bond formation, translocation, E-site exit
Termination at stop codons by release factors
Polyribosome and prokaryotic transcription-translation coupling as context
excluded: Detailed kinetic rate constants beyond the cited 0.05 s per amino acid
Molecular structures of release factors or elongation factors
Selenocysteine/pyrrolysine recoding mechanisms beyond noting exceptions
Eukaryotic initiation factor details beyond Met-tRNAi P-site entry

scientific_entities.description: Messenger RNA carrying codons read 5' to 3' by the ribosome
Small ribosomal subunit (30S in E. coli, 40S in eukaryotes) that binds mRNA
Large ribosomal subunit (50S in E. coli, 60S in eukaryotes) that binds tRNAs and contains peptidyl transferase
Assembled ribosome with A, P, and E sites for tRNA binding
Aminoacyl-tRNA carrying a specific amino acid and an anticodon
Special initiator tRNA carrying fMet in bacteria or Met in eukaryotes that enters the P site directly
Nascent polypeptide chain linked to P-site tRNA and extended by peptide bond formation
Protein that recognizes stop codons in the A site and triggers polypeptide release
Proteins that help the initiation complex assemble correctly
Leader sequence upstream of the first AUG in E. coli mRNA that base-pairs with rRNA to anchor the 30S subunit

required_processes.description: Formation of the initiation complex: small subunit, mRNA, initiator tRNA, initiation factors, GTP; then large subunit joins
tRNA anticodon bonds with mRNA codon through complementary base pairing
Repeated cycle of charged tRNA entry at A site, peptide bond formation, translocation, and E-site tRNA release
Peptidyl transferase catalyzes bond between A-site amino acid amino group and P-site amino acid carboxyl group
Ribosome advances by three bases in the 3' direction, shifting tRNAs from A to P to E sites
Stop codon in A site is recognized by release factors; polypeptide is released and subunits dissociate
Multiple ribosomes simultaneously translate one mRNA; in prokaryotes this can occur concurrently with transcription

required_observations: Initiation complex includes small subunit, mRNA, initiator tRNA, initiation factors, and GTP before large subunit joins
Initiator tRNA enters P site directly, leaving A site free for the first elongation tRNA
Charged tRNA enters A site and its anticodon pairs with the mRNA codon
Peptide bond forms between A-site and P-site amino acids, catalyzed by peptidyl transferase
Ribosome translocates by three bases in the 3' direction, shifting tRNAs from A to P to E sites
Former P-site tRNA enters E site, detaches from amino acid, and is expelled
Stop codon in A site is recognized by release factors, polypeptide is released, subunits dissociate
mRNA is read 5' to 3' and polypeptide synthesized N terminus to C terminus
E. coli uses fMet-tRNA and Shine-Dalgarno; eukaryotes use Met-tRNAi and 80S ribosome without Shine-Dalgarno in the cited passage

support.quote: At this point, the 50S ribosomal subunit then binds to the initiation complex, forming an intact ribosome.
The A (aminoacyl) site binds incoming charged aminoacyl tRNAs.
The anticodon is a three-nucleotide sequence that bonds with an mRNA codon through complementary base pairing.
During each translocation event, the charged tRNAs enter at the A site, then shift to the P site, and then finally to the E site for removal.
As the ribosome steps across the mRNA, the former P-site tRNA enters the E site, detaches from the amino acid, and is expelled.

In E. coli , this complex involves the small 30S ribosome, the mRNA template, three initiation factors that help the ribosome assemble correctly, guanosine triphosphate (GTP) that acts as an energy source, and a special initiator tRNA carrying N -formyl-methionine(fMet-tRNA fMet )

During initiation complex formation, bacterial fMet−tRNA fMet or eukaryotic Met-tRNAi enters the P site directly without first entering the A site, providing a free A site ready to accept the tRNA corresponding to the first codon after the AUG.

In E. coli , the small subunit is described as 30S (which contains the 16S rRNA subunit), and the large subunit is 50S (which contains the 5S and 23S rRNA subunits), for a total of 70S (Svedberg units are not additive).
The amino acid bound to the P-site tRNA is also linked to the growing polypeptide chain.
The P (peptidyl) site binds charged tRNAs carrying amino acids that have formed peptide bonds with the growing polypeptide chain but have not yet dissociated from their corresponding tRNA.

Each mRNA molecule is simultaneously translated by many ribosomes, all synthesizing protein in the same direction: reading the mRNA from 5’ to 3’ and synthesizing the polypeptide from the N terminus to the C terminus.

On aligning with the A site, these nonsense codons are recognized by release factors in prokaryotes and eukaryotes that result in the P-site amino acid detaching from its tRNA, releasing the newly made polypeptide.
The small and large ribosomal subunits dissociate from the mRNA and from each other; they are recruited almost immediately into another translation init iation complex.

exceptions.note: Shine-Dalgarno sequence not described for eukaryotes in cited passage

support.quote: In E. coli mRNA, a leader sequence upstream of the first AUG codon, called the Shine-Dalgarno sequence (also known as the ribosomal binding site AGGAGG), interacts through complementary base pairing with the rRNA molecules that compose the ribosome.
This interaction anchors the 30S ribosomal subunit at the correct location on the mRNA template.
